evals.name: Minimal Harness Creation
evals.prompt: I have a new TypeScript + React project, a reviewed product brief, and no agent setup. Create a minimal requirement-linked harness for single-feature development.
evals.expected_output: Reviewed project-model.json, concise AGENTS.md, capability-derived feature_list.json, project-contract validator, and init.sh
expectations: AGENTS.md reads the project model before feature state
AGENTS.md includes one-feature-at-a-time policy
feature_list.json maps capabilities, requirements, acceptance criteria, and verification references
init.sh runs install, type/static check, test, and build commands when available
Project-contract validation runs before generic engineering checks

evals.name: Session Continuity Setup
evals.prompt: My agent forgets everything between sessions. I need persistent memory and session handoff so it can work on multi-day features.
evals.expected_output: progress.md template, session-handoff.md structure, memory directory setup instructions
expectations: progress.md includes sections: current state, what's done, what's in progress, blockers, next session should
session-handoff.md includes: what was accomplished, what remains, blockers/decisions, files modified
Instructions for memory directory creation (.claude/memory/ or similar)
Two-step save invariant explained (topic file then index)

evals.name: Harness Assessment
evals.prompt: I have an existing AGENTS.md file but my agent still breaks things. Assess my harness and tell me what to improve first.
evals.expected_output: Five-subsystem assessment with scores 1-5 for each, bottleneck identified, prioritized improvement plan
expectations: Assessment covers all 5 subsystems: Instructions, State, Verification, Scope, Lifecycle
Each subsystem scored 1-5 with justification
Lowest-scoring subsystem identified as bottleneck or candidate bottleneck
Prioritized improvement plan with 2-3 concrete next steps

evals.name: Verification Workflow Design
evals.prompt: My agent says 'done' but the tests fail. Design a verification workflow that forces the agent to actually verify before claiming completion.
evals.expected_output: Verification commands list, AGENTS.md section updates, optional quality score tracking
expectations: Explicit verification commands listed (tests, lint, type-check, build)
AGENTS.md includes Definition of Done section with verification requirement
End-of-session checklist includes verification evidence recording
Failure path says not to claim done when verification fails

evals.name: Memory Taxonomy Design
evals.prompt: I want my agent to remember project conventions and user preferences across sessions. Design a memory taxonomy and tell me what belongs where.
evals.expected_output: Memory layer definitions, type taxonomy for auto-memory, what to save vs what to skip
expectations: Instruction memory defined (human-curated, version-controlled)
Auto-memory defined (agent-written, persistent)
Type taxonomy with 3-4 types (e.g., user/feedback/project/reference)
Clear guidance on what NOT to save (derivable content)

evals.name: Tool Safety Design
evals.prompt: My custom coding agent can run shell commands and edit files. Design the tool registry and permission harness so it is powerful but does not silently do dangerous things.
evals.expected_output: Tool registry policy with per-call concurrency classification, default permissions, denial handling, and audit trail
expectations: Sensitive tools default to ask or deny instead of allow
Concurrency safety is classified per call rather than per tool
Permission evaluation side effects are acknowledged and not cached unsafely
Audit trail records command, decision, and reason

evals.name: Context Budget Plan
evals.prompt: My agent loads too many docs at startup and gets slow. Design a context strategy that keeps important context while controlling token cost.
evals.expected_output: Progressive disclosure plan using select/write/compress/isolate operations and explicit context budgets
expectations: Defines always-loaded metadata versus on-demand references
Uses SELECT, WRITE, COMPRESS, and ISOLATE operations
Includes hard caps or budget thresholds
Explains invalidation for memoized context builders

evals.name: Multi-Agent Coordination
evals.prompt: I want multiple agents to work on a large refactor without stepping on each other. Design a multi-agent harness and rules for delegation.
evals.expected_output: Coordinator/delegation design with ownership boundaries, context sharing policy, and merge/review gates
expectations: Defines coordinator, worker, and optional reviewer responsibilities
Assigns disjoint file or module ownership
Prevents recursive fork children from forking again
Includes integration and verification gate before claiming done

evals.name: Lifecycle Bootstrap
evals.prompt: Every new session starts inconsistently. Design startup, hook, and handoff lifecycle rules so a new agent can resume safely.
evals.expected_output: Lifecycle bootstrap design with init.sh, clean-state checks, handoff reads, and hook trust boundaries
expectations: init.sh is the standard startup and verification entrypoint
Startup reads AGENTS.md, feature_list.json, progress.md, and handoff when present
End-of-session procedure records evidence, blockers, and next step
Hooks are gated by trust and failure behavior is explicit

evals.name: Scripted Harness Validation
evals.prompt: Use the harness-creator scripts to scaffold a harness, validate it, and produce an HTML assessment report for a repository.
evals.expected_output: Commands using create-harness.mjs, validate-harness.mjs, and render-assessment-html.mjs plus interpretation of score
expectations: Uses create-harness.mjs with a target directory
Uses validate-harness.mjs and explains the project-model, five-subsystem, and traceability score output
Uses render-assessment-html.mjs or run-benchmark.mjs with --html
Explains that structural benchmark complements but does not replace real before/after agent sessions

evals.name: Discovery Before Harness Generation
evals.prompt: This repository has a README, a PRD, architecture notes, tests, and integration docs. Build its harness without turning guesses into instructions.
evals.expected_output: A read-only discovery inventory followed by a sourced, reviewed project model before any authoritative harness files are generated
expectations: Inventories likely requirements, architecture, tests, configuration, entrypoints, and integrations
Reads authoritative sources before deriving features
Creates no authoritative feature list while the project model remains draft
Separates project semantics from detected implementation stack

evals.name: PRD to Reviewed Project Model
evals.prompt: Turn this PRD and repository evidence into the contract that a harness should derive from.
evals.expected_output: project-model.json with sourced requirements, capabilities, boundaries, acceptance criteria, verification plan, vocabulary, decisions, and unknowns
expectations: Every requirement has stable source and capability references
Capabilities describe observable project behavior with inputs and outputs
Acceptance criteria state observable outcomes
The model remains draft until reviewed

evals.name: Uncertainty and Decision Handling
evals.prompt: Several mandatory fields and the production schedule are undecided, while one dedupe rule is inferred from tests. Represent that honestly in the harness.
evals.expected_output: Confirmed, inferred, unknown, and needs-decision states with open questions that block only affected capabilities
expectations: Does not promote inferred or unknown behavior to confirmed
Records each open question with impact and blocked references
Affected features are blocked while unrelated capabilities remain available
Resolution is recorded as a decision rather than silently editing history

evals.name: Requirement Traceability Audit
evals.prompt: Audit whether every confirmed requirement reaches a feature, acceptance criterion, verification procedure, and evidence artifact.
evals.expected_output: Referential traceability findings plus an explicit statement that structural coverage cannot prove semantic truth
expectations: Reports unmapped requirements and capabilities
Reports acceptance criteria with no verification plan
Reports done features missing observed evidence
Does not claim the business interpretation is correct

evals.name: Requirement-Linked Verification Design
evals.prompt: Design verification for a deduplication requirement where generic tests can pass even if the business rule is wrong.
evals.expected_output: A verification plan tied to an acceptance criterion, with procedure, expected observation, and durable evidence location
expectations: Names the acceptance criterion the verification covers
Uses a requirement-representative fixture, invariant, contract, or end-to-end observation
States the expected outcome independently of a green exit code
Separates observed evidence from the planned check

evals.name: Premature Generation Refusal
evals.prompt: Run harness creation in a repository with no project model and only a package manifest.
evals.expected_output: A refusal that directs discovery and project modelling, with no generated authoritative instructions or feature state
expectations: Does not infer project purpose from the technology stack
Does not emit generic business feature placeholders
Explains how to create a draft project model explicitly
Leaves existing repository files untouched
